english.html: one who kept at his side for these ends during his sickness x. Added to which, the attestation of this kind of people, who by their own confession are perjured and infamous y, ought not to be received, except insofar as, by the circumstances of the business, the judge might be moved to give them some credit and belief z. On which subject Marcus Cicero somewhere says that when someone has once perjured himself, he must not afterwards be believed, nor any credit given him, even though he should swear by several gods a. Thus then, to return to our track: if one who, by testament or other disposition made at the hour when he thinks to die, confesses to owe Jean or Pierre a hundred écus by friendly loan or by deposit, this confession, in truth, inasmuch as it is made in the absence of the party, cannot bring him loss as long as he lives b, but he may freely and without any difficulty whatever retract it c. True it is that if he does not expressly revoke it, that suffices after his death to compel the heir to render to the said Jean or Pierre the said hundred écus confessed d (singularly if such declaration or confession was made for the discharge of conscience e); yes, even though such confession were made by the husband in favour of his wife f — between whom, however, and the husband, gifts, as everyone knows, are not tolerated nor received g. Accursius says further, in some other place, that if the testator confesses to have received from Jean or Pierre a hundred écus by friendly loan, the heir from whom Jean or Pierre demand them cannot oppose to them the exception which we call "of money not counted out" [non numeratae pecuniae], inasmuch as there is no occasion whatever to think that one who thinks to die on the instant, or shortly after, has made such a confession in the hope that the said sum of a hundred écus would afterwards be counted out and paid to him h. And if anyone here wished to say that such a confession, although made by one who thinks to die, does not prove the debt, even were that confession confirmed by oaths i, he [Accursius] answers and confesses that from such a declaration sufficient proof cannot be gathered

l'atteſtation de telle maniere de gens, leſquels par leur
propre confeſſion ſont pariures & infames {y}, ne doit e-
ſtre receuë: ſi ce n'eſt entant que par les circonſtances
du negoce, le iuge pourroit eſtre eſmeu à leur donner
quelque foy, & creance {z}. Sur lequel propos M. Cicerõ
en quelque lieu dit, que quand quelqu'vn ſ'eſt vne fois
pariuré, il ne luy faut apres croire, ne donner foy au-
cune, encore qu'il iuraſt par pluſieurs dieux {a}. Par ainſi
donc, pour reprendre nos briſees, ſi celuy qui par teſta-
ment, ou autre diſpoſition faite ſur l'heure qu'il penſe
mourir, confeſſe deuoir à Iean, ou à Pierre, cent eſcus
d'amiable preſt, ou par deppoſt: ceſte confeſſion, à la
verité, d'autant qu'elle eſt faite partie abſente, ne peut
luy porter dommage tant qu'il viura {b}. ains la pourra
librement & ſans difficulté quelcõque retracter {c}. vray
que ſi nommément il ne la reuoque, cela ſuffit apres
ſa mort, pour cõtraindre l'heritier à rendre audit Iean,
ou à Pierre, leſdits cent eſcus confeſſez {d}. (Singuliere-
ment ſi telle declaration, ou confeſſiõ a eſté faite pour
la deſcharge de la conſcience {e}). voire encore que telle
confeſſion fut faite par le mari, au profit de ſa femme {f}.
Entre laquelle pourtant, & le mari, les donnaiſons. cõ-
me chacun ſçait, ne ſont tolerees, ni receuës {g}. dit d'auan
tage Accurſe en quelque autre lieu, que ſi le teſtateur
confeſſe auoir receu de Iean, ou de Pierre cent eſcus
par amiable preſt, l'heritier à qui Iean, ou Pierre les de-
mande, ne leur pourra oppoſer l'exceptiõ que nous ap-
pellons de pecune non nombree. d'autãt qu'il n'y a oc-
caſion aucune, de penſer que celuy qui ſur l'heure, ou
peu apres penſe mourir, ayt fait telle confeſſion, ſous
eſperance qu'on luy cõpaſt; & payaſt apres ladite ſom-
me de cent eſcus {h}. Et ſi quelqu'vn vouloit ici dire, que
telle confeſſion, bien que ſoit faite par celuy qui penſe
mourir, ne preuue point la debte, ou fuſt icelle cõfeſſiõ
confirmee par ermens {i}: il reſpond & confeſſe que de
